body:
You can simplify your formula a bit to make it cheaper, avoid the division, and clarify what it is actually doing. 

`mix(x, y, a)` is implemented like `x * (1−a) + y * a`

You have changed it to basically `x * (1-a) + (y / a) * a`

Which can be simplified to `x * (1-a) + y`. Basically you are darkening the sky color by the density of the fog and then adding the fog color on top.

I can confirm that I also see a dark outline.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/70922c51-0b4f-4ad0-b55f-665d96b0d61d)

I think we shouldn't use a workaround inside the editor to prevent this, maybe a separate option should be provided to enable this outline, as this effect is sometimes useful.

This isn't a new issue to my knowledge - I remember seeing it in 4.0.alpha already.

The proposed solution makes sense to me. We'll just need to make sure it behaves well in peculiar scenarios (e.g. FogVolume with density above `1`, overbright fog colors and so on).

Testing project: [test-volumetric-fog-dense.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18466706/test-volumetric-fog-dense.zip)

Well, I think we just need to check what the correct blending equation is.

_edit: premultiplied blending appears to be correct (see https://bartwronski.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/08/bwronski_volumetric_fog_siggraph2014.pdf)_

> Well, I think we just need to check what the correct blending equation is.

I've compared the above testing project before and after the change proposed in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/101514#issuecomment-2589015575:

master | Proposed change
-|-
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/edec530f-2536-48bc-9051-a426488315af) | ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/406c0d8e-bfe6-4a5d-9436-5c36a53a09cb)

This looks better to me overall - the dark halos around the edges are gone. The fog seems a bit brighter as a consequence of this change, especially around the edges (but the middle isn't affected much). However, this change also makes aliasing more visible even though temporal reprojection is enabled in both cases (I waited 30 frames before taking a screenshot to let it converge).

Note that the proposed change removes the influence of `fog_sky_affect`, which is incorrect as we should keep it as part of the equation. A value of `0.0` makes it not affect the sky at all, `1.0` makes it act like the proposed change, and intermediate values should blend between both states.
@shakesoda Please go ahead and make a PR!
